subject: Performance qualification: k6 handoff & account provisioning for streaming SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Ross <julia.ross@acmetech.com>, Acme Tech Eng Team <engineering@acmetech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance qualification: k6 handoff & account provisioning for streaming SLOs

Hi Julia (and Acme eng/ops),

Thanks again for a great discovery call today. Quick recap so we have a single place to track next steps for the performance/SLO qualification and the customer-led load rehearsal you requested. High-level asks you confirmed:

- Target P99 latency: <= 220ms for single-turn streaming responses (up to 512 tokens).
- Sustain throughput: 220 concurrent streaming connections with ~8 tokens/sec average output per connection.
- Burst window: allow short bursts to 400 concurrent streams for 2–3 minutes.
- Test types: steady-state concurrency run (k6), and one burst rehearsal (Locust/locustfile optional).

What we need from Acme to proceed:
1) A test account for Redwood to verify model routing and token billing behavior (API key or ephemeral token) OR provide a test key for your engineers to run scripts.
2) IP allowlist: a CSV of destination IP ranges we should whitelist on your firewall (we included a template attachment).
3) Preferred test window (three options from your side so we can coordinate Dedicated capacity).
4) Any additional streaming constraints (max simultaneous open sockets per client, proxy timeouts).

Action items and owners:
- Acme: provide test account/keys and firewall team contact (Julia) — due Wed 08/25.
- Redwood (Marissa): share k6 scripts + runbook, access instructions, and sample SLO matrix (attached).
- Redwood (Rishi): stand up a monitoring slice during the run and capture token-level latencies and failure reasons.
- Redwood (Ben): coordinate capacity (reserved burst) and front-line on-call for the rehearsal window.

Attachments: acme-k6-scripts.tar.gz (k6 scenario + environment variables stub), network-allowlist-template.csv, slo-matrix.xlsx

If the above matches your notes, please reply with your preferred test window (dates/times in CDT or UTC) and whether you want Redwood to run the scripts or you'd rather run them from your environment with our guidance.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cope@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0133
Redwood Inference

---
Potential follow-up: I can provision a temporary k6 cloud run if you want a quick smoke before the full rehearsal.
From: Julia Ross <julia.ross@acmetech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Acme Tech Eng Team <engineering@acmetech.com>
Cc: Acme Ops <ops@acmetech.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance qualification: k6 handoff & account provisioning for streaming SLOs

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the high-level targets look right to Acme leadership. A few clarifications from our infra side:

- P99 measured at the edge (ingress) for the streaming socket handshake + first token should be <= 220ms; we'll include downstream egress checks but primary SLO is ingress.
- Our clients open up to 4 sockets per instance; we will limit to 2 per instance for the test unless Redwood suggests otherwise.
- We can run the k6 scripts from our environment; please provide env var names and sample values for auth and endpoint.

We will:
- Share firewall contact + allowlist slot by tomorrow (ops@acmetech.com).
- Propose test windows: Tue 08/31 17:00–19:00 UTC, Wed 09/01 02:00–04:00 UTC, or Thu 09/02 22:00–00:00 UTC.

We prefer to run from our env but would appreciate Redwood standing by to validate metrics and help interpret failed requests.

— Julia
Julia Ross | Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Tech
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Ross <julia.ross@acmetech.com>, Acme Tech Eng Team <engineering@acmetech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance qualification: k6 handoff & account provisioning for streaming SLOs

Perfect — thanks Julia. Two quick operational notes before the run:

1) k6 environment variables: see attached run variables in acme-k6-scripts.tar.gz. Key names we use: REDWOOD_API_HOST, REDWOOD_TEST_KEY (or API_KEY), TEST_ACCOUNT_ID, K6_VUS, K6_DURATION. We will include a sample .env file inside the tar.

2) Allowlist process: please populate the network-allowlist-template.csv with your firewall's accepted range format and send to ops@redwood.ai AND cc ops@acmetech.com so we can validate on our side. If you prefer, Ben will schedule a 20-minute networking handoff call with your firewall engineer.

Operational support: Rishi will collect token-level traces and publish a short metrics report within 2 hours after the rehearsal. Ben — can you confirm Dedicated pool + burst reservation for Wed 09/01 02:00–04:00 UTC (this is the customer's preferred middle option)?

If Acrobat or DocuSign is required for a temporary NDA/PO to enable the run, let us know — we can fast-track.

Regards,
Marissa

Attachment notes: acme-k6-scripts.tar.gz contains k6 scenario (streaming-sim.js), env samples, and a short README with run commands. slo-matrix.xlsx is a starter with baseline targets and measurement points.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Julia Ross <julia.ross@acmetech.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance qualification: k6 handoff & account provisioning for streaming SLOs

All — Ben here. Confirmed: I reserved a Dedicated capacity slice for Wed 09/01 02:00–04:00 UTC with a burst allowance to 450 concurrent streams for up to 3 minutes. I'll keep the slice attached to deal ACME-2027-013 so billing is isolated.

Network handoff: I'm happy to run a 20m call with your firewall engineer. Julia — can you send the firewall contact and available 20m slots? Otherwise we can validate the allowlist once you send the CSV.

I'll be on-call during the window; Rishi will publish the post-run token latency report. If we see steady P99 > 220ms we'll capture packet errors and inspect kernel metrics — plan is to fail open to a compatible lower-latency variant if it helps your users during burst testing.

— Ben
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Acme Ops <ops@acmetech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Ross <julia.ross@acmetech.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance qualification: k6 handoff & account provisioning for streaming SLOs

Ben/Marissa/Rishi — ops here. Attached is the filled allowlist CSV (network-allowlist-template.csv) and our short firewall contact: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@acmetech.com>. Miguel is available Tue 08/30 16:00–18:00 UTC or Wed 08/31 13:00–15:00 UTC for a quick 20-minute handoff.

We will run the k6 scripts from our infra; REDWOOD_TEST_KEY placeholder is set in the env sample. Expect a smoke run Tue 08/31 17:00–17:15 UTC and the full rehearsal Wed 09/01 02:00–04:00 UTC.

Thanks — ops
